## 1. `def:cover` — definition: Cover with running intersection (`TTH-01`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-01; label: def:cover -->

Digest: [4. TTH-01: `acyclicLocalWitnessGluing`; TTN-08: cyclic obstruction](formal_digest.md#4-tth-01-acycliclocalwitnessgluing-ttn-08-cyclic-obstruction)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_04_checks.tex:17`.

```latex
A \emph{cover} is a family of pieces, each with a scope (the cells it reads),
such that every cell lies in some scope, together with an adjacency relation
on pieces. It has the \emph{running-intersection} property if any two pieces
whose scopes contain a cell $c$ are joined by a path of adjacent pieces whose
scopes all contain $c$. Local assignments are \emph{compatible along edges} if
adjacent pieces assign the same value to every cell they share.
```

</td><td valign="top">

#### `CSTTT.PackageTheory.acyclicLocalWitnessGluing`

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Classical.choice`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean
@CSTTT.PackageTheory.acyclicLocalWitnessGluing : {Index Coord Value : Type} →
  (tree : CSTTT.PackageTheory.RootedJoinTree Index Coord) →
    (localAssignment : Index → Coord → Value) →
      (accepted hardGate : Index → Prop) →
        (∀ (i j : Index) (c : Coord),
            tree.adjacent i j → tree.scope i c → tree.scope j c → localAssignment i c = localAssignment j c) →
          (∀ (i : Index), accepted i) →
            (∀ (i : Index), hardGate i) →
              CSTTT.PackageTheory.IntegratedPackageWitness tree localAssignment accepted hardGate
```

</table>

```latex

assignments be compatible along edges. Then there is a global assignment whose
restriction to each piece's scope is that piece's local assignment.
```

## 3. `prop:cycle` — proposition: Agreement between neighbours is not enough (`TTN-08`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTN-08; label: prop:cycle -->

Digest: [4. TTH-01: `acyclicLocalWitnessGluing`; TTN-08: cyclic obstruction](formal_digest.md#4-tth-01-acycliclocalwitnessgluing-ttn-08-cyclic-obstruction)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_04_checks.tex:52`.

```latex
On the target of the two-copy model there are eight local assignments, one for
each condition, each accepted and gated by its own condition, such that
adjacent pieces agree on every cell they share, where adjacency forms a cycle
through the eight conditions. Yet no global assignment restricts to all eight.
```

</td><td valign="top">

## 5. `def:handoff` — definition: Strict handoff (`TTH-04`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-04; label: def:handoff -->

Digest: [3. TTH-04: `strictTemporalCorridorComposition_generic`](formal_digest.md#3-tth-04-stricttemporalcorridorcomposition_generic)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_04_checks.tex:98`.

```latex
A handoff is \emph{strict} if it passes every check of the formal atomic
gate, expanded in Appendix~\ref{app:checks}. In summary, the gate
requires the following.
\begin{itemize}
\item Source and target are distinct, and there are at least three stages.
\item Only the source is live at entry and only the target at exit.
\item Some stage has both live: this is the overlap.
\item Every stage is realized, so there is no gap.
\item Each step from one stage to the next increases order, tick, progress
and records by a strictly positive amount, extends the route memory, and keeps
an owner among the live systems.
\item Events have unique identifiers, valid stages and owners, and their
dependencies point forward.
\item Every stage has a nonempty maintenance state.
\item An intervention check shows that both systems' contributions are needed,
and an audit check holds.
\item The route is recorded as route-indexed.
\end{itemize}
A \emph{strict chain} is a nonempty list of strict handoffs in which each
handoff ends exactly where the next begins: the same intermediate system and
the same boundary stage, including its whole frontier. Its first source and
last target must differ.
```

</td><td valign="top">

#### `CSTTT.CorridorTheory.AtomicChain.strictTemporalCorridorComposition_generic`

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `propext`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean

  (legs : List CSTTT.CorridorTheory.AtomicChain.FiniteAtomicLeg),
  CSTTT.CorridorTheory.AtomicChain.CorridorPass legs → CSTTT.CorridorTheory.AtomicChain.StrictCorridorWitness legs
```

</td></tr>
</table>

## 8. `prop:gap` — proposition: Gap (`TTN-09`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTN-09; label: prop:gap -->

```latex
On the two-copy model, if one overlap stage is removed from the realized
episode, the source and target stages remain realized, the steps remain
strict, the two routes' endpoints agree, and source and target have equal
predictive readouts at the endpoint. Yet the episode fails the no-gap
condition, and the handoff is not strict.
```

## 10. `def:autonomy` — definition: Autonomy certificate (`TTH-05`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-05; label: def:autonomy -->

Digest: [5. TTH-05: `postWithdrawalFiniteHorizonInvariance` and `ExactAutonomyCertificate`](formal_digest.md#5-tth-05-postwithdrawalfinitehorizoninvariance-and-exactautonomycertificate)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_04_checks.tex:188`.

```latex
Fix a finite controlled system with disturbances and actions, a region of its
states, and a list of withdrawn and retained resources. An \emph{autonomy
certificate} states the following.
\begin{itemize}
\item The withdrawals are made and fixed before evaluation.
\item The target's endpoint lies in the region.
\item Every state in the region realizes the target's conditions.
\item Maintenance uses only retained resources, all owned by the target.
\item For every state in the region and every disturbance, there is an action
owned by the target whose result stays in the region, does not stall, and
remains within budget.
\end{itemize}
```

</td><td valign="top">

## 16. `def:certificate` — definition: Continuation certificate (`TTH-06-GEN`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-06-GEN; label: def:certificate -->

Digest: [1. TTH-06: generic Temporal-FIACH soundness (F and O), and the POS-04 instance](formal_digest.md#1-tth-06-generic-temporal-fiach-soundness-f-and-o-and-the-pos-04-instance)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_05_continuation.tex:23`.

```latex
A handoff model with a source assignment passes the \emph{continuation
certificate} if every check of the formal gate holds. Appendix~\ref{app:checks}
expands the gate component by component. In summary, the gate requires the following.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Source.} The source assignment satisfies the eight conditions on
the source.
\item \emph{Realization.} The mapped pieces satisfy the cover, scope,
totality and value-preservation checks. Each is accepted by its own condition
on the target, and adjacent pieces agree where they overlap.
\item \emph{Lineage.} For every route of the episode the computed handoffs
form a strict chain (Definition~\ref{def:handoff}). The predictive and
record readouts of source and target are related by the declared transport.
Within each of the two systems, states with the same predictive code have the
same observation laws for every finite sequence of actions. The translation
from source to target commutes with initial states, transition weights,
successors and observations on the whole set of source states the execution
reaches. The typed endpoint obligations and the coherence of the shared
runtime also hold, including the temporal condition's decoder.
\item \emph{Autonomy.} After every declared role is withdrawn, a game
invariant certificate (Lemma~\ref{lem:strategy}) covers the target's runs. It
is a stronger object than the finite certificate of
Definition~\ref{def:autonomy}: it ranges over full run histories, and it
requires normalized responses in the stated sparse format, legal moves using
only the target's own retained resources, and strict advance of order, tick,
progress and records. In the \emph{realization-preserving} version the
invariant includes the target's realization. In the \emph{operational}
version it requires only membership in a declared part of the target's state
space.
\item \emph{Bookkeeping.} The route is recorded as route-indexed, and the
receiver of the source's content passes its own content and intervention
checks.
\end{enumerate}
```

</td><td valign="top">

## 17. `thm:continuation` — theorem: Continuation theorem (`TTH-06-GEN`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-06-GEN; label: thm:continuation -->

Digest: [1. TTH-06: generic Temporal-FIACH soundness (F and O), and the POS-04 instance](formal_digest.md#1-tth-06-generic-temporal-fiach-soundness-f-and-o-and-the-pos-04-instance)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_05_continuation.tex:62`.

```latex
Let a handoff model with a source assignment pass the continuation certificate
in its realization-preserving version. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(R)] \emph{Realization.} The computed target assignment is total,
restricts to every mapped piece on its scope, and is accepted by all eight
conditions on the target.
\item[(L)] \emph{Lineage.} For every route the computed handoffs form a
strict chain. Moreover, within the source and within the target, any two
states with the same predictive code give the same probability to every finite
sequence of observations under every finite sequence of actions.
\item[(A)] \emph{Autonomy.} After withdrawal there is a strategy for the target
such that every history it generates, from every genuine entry state and
following every outcome of positive probability, stays realized, uses only the
target's own retained resources, makes only legal and affordable moves, and
strictly advances order, tick, progress and records at every step.
\end{enumerate}
In the operational version, (R) and (L) hold as stated, and (A) holds with
``stays realized'' replaced by ``stays in the declared part of the state
space''.
```

</td><td valign="top">

#### `CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.FinalHandoff.temporalFIACHCertificateSoundness_generic_F`

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `propext`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean
  [inst_5 : DecidableEq Id] [inst_6 : DecidableEq Owner] [inst_7 : DecidableEq Resource] [inst_8 : DecidableEq P]
  [inst_9 : DecidableEq Q]
  (m :
    CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.FinalHandoff.Raw SC Cell SourceValue Value R SR TR RV SRV TRV S A O H HF Route
      Stage Id Owner D P Q Factor Resource Endpoint)
  (a : CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.Assignment SC SourceValue),
  CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.FinalHandoff.HandoffPass_F m a →
```

## 18. `lem:lumping` — lemma: From one step to every future (`TTH-06-GEN`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-06-GEN; label: lem:lumping -->

Digest: [1. TTH-06: generic Temporal-FIACH soundness (F and O), and the POS-04 instance](formal_digest.md#1-tth-06-generic-temporal-fiach-soundness-f-and-o-and-the-pos-04-instance)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_05_continuation.tex:89`.

```latex
Consider a system with a finite list of outcomes, and suppose any two states
with the same code satisfy three conditions. They have the same observation.
For every action and every outcome, they move to states with the same code.
For every action, they give equal total weight to each code class of next
states. Then any two states with the same code give the same probability to
every finite sequence of observations, under every finite sequence of
actions.
```

</td><td valign="top">

## 19. `lem:strategy` — lemma: From an invariant to a strategy (`TTH-06-GEN`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-06-GEN; label: lem:strategy -->

Digest: [1. TTH-06: generic Temporal-FIACH soundness (F and O), and the POS-04 instance](formal_digest.md#1-tth-06-generic-temporal-fiach-soundness-f-and-o-and-the-pos-04-instance)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_05_continuation.tex:101`.

```latex
Suppose an invariant set of runs satisfies the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item The withdrawal holds, and some entry run exists.
\item Every entry lies in the invariant.
\item Every run in the invariant satisfies the realization predicate and the
resource conditions.
\item For every run in the invariant and every disturbance, some legal action
has normalized outcome weights (nonnegative, summing to one, with a positive
entry), and each outcome of positive weight leads to a run in the invariant
and satisfies the transition law.
\end{itemize}
Then there is a causal strategy under which every history generated from every
entry consists of runs satisfying the realization predicate and the resource
conditions. At each of these runs, for every disturbance, the chosen action is
legal and normalized, and each of its positive outcomes satisfies the
transition law.
```

</td><td valign="top">

## 26. `thm:fork` — theorem: Continuation is relation-valued (`TTH-08`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTH-08; label: thm:fork -->

Digest: [6. TTH-08: `native_relation_valued_temporal_fission`; TTN-11](formal_digest.md#6-tth-08-native_relation_valued_temporal_fission-ttn-11)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_07_branching.tex:16`.

```latex
In the symmetric fork of the chain model, labelled
\snapGSevenForkSystemIds{} (source first), the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The source continues to each of the two targets, and the valid targets
are exactly these two. Each carries the chain model's handoff certificate,
covering realization, lineage and autonomy after withdrawal, for every state of
the finite factor.
\item The swap of the two targets preserves validity and is an involution.
\item No continuer is fixed by the swap.
\end{enumerate}
```

</td><td valign="top">

```lean
  CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.NativeComposition.NativeFission.fork.related
      CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.NativeComposition.NativeFission.fork.source
      CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.NativeComposition.NativeFission.fork.right ∧
    (∀ (target : CSTTT.CarrierId),
        CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.NativeComposition.NativeFission.fork.valid target ↔
```

## 28. `thm:identity` — theorem: Ancestry underdetermines identity (`TTF-07`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTF-07; label: thm:identity -->

Digest: [7. TTF-07: `actual_branch_identity_return` and `IdentityUnderdetermined`](formal_digest.md#7-ttf-07-actual_branch_identity_return-and-identityunderdetermined)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_07_branching.tex:64`.

```latex
On the chain model, for every $n$, there is a safe execution of $n+1$ steps
after withdrawal, ending in a fission, in which the source has two descendants
holding the same state. That state passes the model's realization
check, with conditions (4) to (7) in simplified form, and obeys its
continuation law.
Consider identity relations that are equivalences, that identify the source
with at most one other node, and that identify the source with no node other
than itself that is not its descendant under the computed ancestry. Among these there are two that
identify the source with different descendants, and neither identification is
forced.
```

## 31. `prop:reconstruction` — proposition: Reconstruction versus twin (`TTF-06`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTF-06; label: prop:reconstruction -->

<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_08_ancestry.tex:31`.

```latex
In the declared operational controls, suppose a reconstruction is derived
from the source after the source becomes inactive, passing the controls'
snapshot, erasure, gap, activation and bridge-law checks, and an independent
twin has the same content. Then the source is an ancestor of the
reconstruction and not of the twin.
```

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `propext`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean
      (source record target twin duration maxAge : Nat) (payload : S),
      source ≠ record →
        source ≠ target →
          source ≠ twin →
            record ≠ target →
              record ≠ twin →
                target ≠ twin →
                  2 + duration - 1 ≤ maxAge →
                    (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.StructuralAdjudication.RootedReconstructionTwinSeparation Nat Nat
                        (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.ReconstructionRolesPrototype.SameActualTargets b
                          (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.ReconstructionRolesPrototype.rawInputs b source record target twin

                        CSTTT.FallbackTheory.GuardedFusion.actualAncestry b
                            (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.ReconstructionRolesPrototype.rawInputs b source record target twin
                              duration maxAge payload)
                            [] (Option.some program) (Option.some credits) [] root endpoint =
                          Option.some Bool.true) ∧
                      (∀ (sourceDerived : Nat → Nat → Prop),
                          ¬CSTTT.Prospects.DestructiveReconstructionTwinSeparation Nat
                              (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.ReconstructionRolesPrototype.SameActualTargets b
                                (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.ReconstructionRolesPrototype.rawInputs b source record target twin
                                  duration maxAge payload)
                                (Option.some program) (Option.some credits))
                              sourceDerived fun root endpoint =>
                              CSTTT.FallbackTheory.GuardedFusion.actualAncestry b
                                  (CSTTT.FallbackTheory.ReconstructionRolesPrototype.rawInputs b source record target
                                    twin duration maxAge payload)
                                  [] (Option.some program) (Option.some credits) [] root endpoint =
```

```latex
Under the least ancestry relation, fission, guarded fusion and empty outcomes
are characterized as relations. On the fusion model, a guarded fusion has
\snapFullNativeZeroTwoFusionOutcomeCount{} settlement outcomes, with
probabilities \snapFullNativeZeroTwoFusionSettlementProbabilities{}, summing
to \snapFullNativeZeroTwoFusionProbabilitySum{}. Each outcome retires both
```

## 34. `thm:ancestry` — theorem: Continuation by ancestry (`TTF-05`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTF-05; label: thm:ancestry -->

Digest: [8. TTF-05: `original_integrated_temporal_iaps` and `all_actual_outputs_three_lanes`](formal_digest.md#8-ttf-05-original_integrated_temporal_iaps-and-all_actual_outputs_three_lanes)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_08_ancestry.tex:111`.

```latex
On the fusion model, every request of the declared protocol that executes
successfully yields, for the request's owner and from that same execution, the
following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item predictive ancestry from the source;
\item realization of all eight computed conditions;
\item autonomy after withdrawal that preserves that realization.
\end{enumerate}
The successful requests include both children of a fission, after the source
is withdrawn and each child has completed its own local acquisition, and the
output of a guarded fusion after its acquisition. The same three properties
hold for every history retained from an acquired fusion output.
```

## 35. `def:direct` — definition: Direct succession (`TTD-01`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTD-01; label: def:direct -->

Digest item: none matched by claim/source-row ID or headline declaration.

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_09_modes.tex:11`.

```latex
A target event is a \emph{direct successor} of a source event when the pair
passes the computed direct-succession check (Appendix~\ref{app:index}). A
direct successor is generated by that single, necessary source event and
carries the source's whole eight-field frontier, advanced by one strict step.
In addition, the source event is used once only, nothing is stored or replayed
in between, there is no alternative parent, and route and ownership are
transferred correctly.
```

</td><td valign="top">

```lean
    ∃ raw b,
      CSTTT.CorridorTheory.RawDirectSuccessor.directProjection m = Option.some (raw, b) ∧
        Nonempty
          (CSTTT.DirectSuccessorTheory.AtomicDirectSuccessorCertificate
            (CSTTT.CorridorTheory.RawDirectValidity.data raw b m.input))
```

## 37. `prop:direct-exclusions` — proposition: What direct succession excludes (`TTD-03`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTD-03; label: prop:direct-exclusions -->

```latex
The direct criterion excludes four mechanisms: detached copies, replay from an
archive, reconstruction through storage, and gaps. Reachability by data alone
does not make a direct successor. Conversely, a separate data path can coexist
with genuine direct succession.
```

```latex
instances that are not instances of the other. In fact the two modes are
disjoint on every model, since overlap needs the source and target events in
one stage and direct succession needs them in adjacent stages. Both embed in a
broader, separately named relation of continuity paths, in which compatible
mixed paths compose and closed paths are excluded.
```

## 39. `thm:unbounded` — theorem: Unbounded maintenance on a finite factor (`TTS-04`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTS-04; label: thm:unbounded -->

Digest: [11. TTD-02: `actual_modes_incomparable`; TTS-04: `all_supported_streams_infinite_laws`](formal_digest.md#11-ttd-02-actual_modes_incomparable-tts-04-all_supported_streams_infinite_laws)

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_09_modes.tex:65`.

```latex
On the chain model, take the target's computed policy on a finite factor of its
state, with unbounded event registers. Assume that the policy's inputs are
ready, that the initial factor lies in the policy's computed greatest viable
set, and that the initial balance covers the computed reserve. The policy's
responses are owned by the target and normalized, and its positive outcomes
advance and credit at least what they debit. Then for every
admissible stream of disturbances and every stream of outcomes of positive
probability, the resulting infinite run has the following properties at every
step:
\begin{itemize}
\item it stays in the policy's greatest viable set and realizes the
conditions, with (4) to (7) in simplified form;
\item it strictly increases progress and records;
\item it keeps the balance at or above the computed reserve.
\end{itemize}
```

</td><td valign="top">

#### `CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.all_supported_streams_infinite_laws`

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `propext`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean
@CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.all_supported_streams_infinite_laws : ∀ {Cell X D A O : Type}
  {Value : Cell → Type} [inst : DecidableEq X] (m : CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.Raw Cell Value X D A O)
  (a : CSTTT.TargetTheory.GenericHandoff.Assignment Cell Value)
  (h : CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.Ready m a),
  CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.TotalComputedPolicy m a h →
    ∀ (stream : Nat → D) (outcomes : Nat → O),
      CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.SupportedOutcomes m a h stream outcomes →
        ∀ (n : Nat),
          have x := CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.outcomeTrajectory m a h stream outcomes n;
          have y := CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.outcomeTrajectory m a h stream outcomes (n + 1);
          x.factor ∈ CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.greatest m a h ∧
            CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.PackageAt m a x.factor ∧
              CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.StepOf m a h x (stream n) y ∧
                x.progress < y.progress ∧
                  x.record < y.record ∧
                    CSTTT.AutonomyTheory.RawRechargingPolicy.reserve m a h ≤ x.balance ∧ 0 ≤ x.balance
```

## 40. `prop:defects` — proposition: Exact defect semantics (`TTS-02`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTS-02; label: prop:defects -->

Digest item: none matched by claim/source-row ID or headline declaration.

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_09_modes.tex:97`.

```latex
Let each condition carry a labelled rational defect, and require defects and
tolerances to be nonnegative. A profile is accepted exactly when every required
defect is zero and every soft defect is at most its own tolerance. Acceptance is
downward closed, which means that lowering defects while keeping labels, types
and tolerances preserves it. Acceptance is not determined by the total defect sum, since two
profiles with the same schema and the same sum can differ.
```

</td><td valign="top">

#### `CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.exact_acceptance_iff`

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Quot.sound`, `propext`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean
CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.exact_acceptance_iff : ∀ (v : List CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.Component),
  CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.VectorAccepts v ↔
    (∀ (c : CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.Component), c ∈ v → 0 ≤ c.defect ∧ 0 ≤ c.tolerance) ∧
      (∀ (c : CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.Component), c ∈ v → c.hard = Bool.true → c.defect = 0) ∧
        ∀ (c : CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.Component), c ∈ v → c.hard = Bool.false → c.defect ≤ c.tolerance
```

#### `CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.component_downward`

**Axioms (declaration map):** `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, `propext`. **in_inventory:** `yes`.

```lean
CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.component_downward : ∀ (lo hi : CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.Component),
  lo.hard = hi.hard →
    lo.tolerance = hi.tolerance →
      0 ≤ lo.defect →
        lo.defect ≤ hi.defect →
          CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.ComponentAccepts hi → CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.ComponentAccepts lo
```

```lean
        CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.VectorAccepts x ∧ ¬CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.VectorAccepts y
```

```lean
        CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.scalar x = CSTTT.RationalDefectTheory.scalar y ∧
```

## 42. `prop:conditioning` — proposition: Conditioning does not factor (`JOINT-COND`)

<!-- correspondence-claim: JOINT-COND; label: prop:conditioning -->

Digest item: none matched by claim/source-row ID or headline declaration.

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `appendices/app_d_proofs.tex:45`.

```latex
On the predecessor of the fusion model, a shared event has two outcomes, of
weights \snapGTwoSixConditioningEventWeights{} (ratio
\snapGTwoSixConditioningRelativeWeights{}). Conditioned on the event, and with the empty action word, the joint initial
observation associated with the lower-weight outcome has probability
\snapGTwoSixConditionedJointMass{}. Its two components are the corresponding
initial observations of the two branches. Each has conditioned probability
\snapGTwoSixConditionedLeftMass{}, and their product is
\snapGTwoSixProductOfConditionedMarginals{}. The correct joint
law is a weighted sum of products of the branch laws over fixed worlds.
```

</td><td valign="top">

```latex
On the models of Section~\ref{sec:continuation}, a realization on the target is
built in stages. Typed maps carry each condition's cells from the source to
the target. Each mapped piece is then accepted, independently, by its own
condition on the target, and a compatible cover on the target, also checked
independently, glues the pieces. The assembly uses no premise about lineage or autonomy. Realization,
in other words, can be established without knowing how the target came to be.
```

```latex
We first collect what ancestry does and does not give. A \emph{predictive
bridge} between source and target descends to a map between their predictive
classes. That map is unique and does not depend on the choice of
representatives. Starting from admissible seeds of provenance, the records of

ancestry from nothing. Two consequences follow.
```

## 47. Prose-only claim `TTF-02`

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTF-02 -->

Digest item: none matched by claim/source-row ID or headline declaration.

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_08_ancestry.tex:16`.

```latex
We first collect what ancestry does and does not give. A \emph{predictive
bridge} between source and target descends to a map between their predictive
classes. That map is unique and does not depend on the choice of
representatives. Starting from admissible seeds of provenance, the records of
an execution generate a least ancestry relation. Being least, it gives no
ancestry from nothing. Two consequences follow.
```

</td><td valign="top">

## 48. Prose-only claim `TTS-01`

<!-- correspondence-claim: TTS-01 -->

Digest item: none matched by claim/source-row ID or headline declaration.

<table>
<tr><th>Paper statement (LaTeX)</th><th>Lean headline declarations</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

Source: `sections/sec_09_modes.tex:49`.

```latex
Strict overlap continuation and direct succession are incomparable. Each has
instances that are not instances of the other. In fact the two modes are
disjoint on every model, since overlap needs the source and target events in
one stage and direct succession needs them in adjacent stages. Both embed in a
broader, separately named relation of continuity paths, in which compatible
mixed paths compose and closed paths are excluded.
```

</td><td valign="top">
